blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin degludec FlexTouch concentration and dose-conversion safety
stem: An adult who uses TRESIBA U-100 FlexTouch is changed to the U-200 FlexTouch pen. The prescribed dose remains 40 units once daily. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.A: Dial 40 units on the U-200 FlexTouch pen; the dose window displays the insulin units to deliver, so no concentration-based dose conversion is needed.
options.B: Dial 20 units on the U-200 FlexTouch pen because the concentration is doubled and the prescribed 40-unit dose must be divided by two.
options.C: Dial 80 units on the U-200 FlexTouch pen because the higher concentration requires doubling the displayed units to preserve the prescribed dose.
options.D: Withdraw the U-200 insulin from the FlexTouch pen into an insulin syringe and calculate the equivalent syringe volume before each injection.

rationale: Current TRESIBA prescribing information states not to perform dose conversion when using the U-100 or U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window displays the number of insulin units to be delivered. Therefore a prescription for 40 units is dialed as 40 units on the U-200 pen. B and C apply incorrect concentration-based conversions. D is unsafe and contradicts the label, which states not to transfer TRESIBA from a FlexTouch pen into a syringe because dosing errors and severe hypoglycemia can result.
educational_objective: When switching between TRESIBA U-100 and U-200 FlexTouch pens, use the prescribed number of insulin units shown in the dose window without manual dose conversion and do not withdraw insulin from the pen into a syringe.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); TRESIBA prescribing information
source_document_title: TRESIBA (insulin degludec) injection, for subcutaneous use — Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Revised July 2026; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §2.2 General Dosing Instructions: TRESIBA is available as U-100 and U-200; 'DO NOT perform dose conversion' when using U-100 or U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window shows the number of insulin units to be delivered. §2.1 Important Administration Instructions and §5.4 Hypoglycemia Due to Medication Errors: do not transfer TRESIBA from the FlexTouch pen into a syringe because dosing errors/overdose and severe hypoglycemia can result.
source_claim_supported: TRESIBA U-100 and U-200 FlexTouch pens require no manual dose conversion because the dose window displays actual insulin units; insulin should not be withdrawn from the pen into a syringe.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; prepare and administer medications using rights of medication administration; perform calculations needed for medication administration; educate clients about medications; handle and administer high-risk medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt the item as an applied U-100 to U-200 FlexTouch dose-safety scenario instead of a broad fact-recall statement.
Rewrote all four options as parallel dosing instructions of comparable length and removed isolated absolute-word cues.
Focused the keyed response on one exact label rule: the displayed units are the units delivered, so no manual concentration conversion is performed.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely follows current §2.2 labeling. B and C perform prohibited manual concentration conversions in opposite directions, and D conflicts with the explicit prohibition on withdrawing TRESIBA from a FlexTouch pen into a syringe. No second defensible answer, hidden assumption, or material cueing remains.
